To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a DNA repair variant in the Pol θ gene (c.-1061A >  G) is associated with hereditary (HBOC syndrome) and bilateral breast cancer patients.
a DNA repair gene variant is associated with hereditary bilateral breast cancer.
a DNA repair variant in the POLQ gene is associated with hereditary and bilateral breast cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genetic markers associated to POLQ, a gene involved in DNA repair, as new biomarkers of risk for hereditary breast cancer.
the identification of genetic biomarkers of risk for HBC.
the identification of new genetic markers for the early diagnosis and prevention of hereditary breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SNP c.-1060A>G of POLQ is associated with hereditary (HBOC syndrome) and sporadic bilateral breast cancer patients.
the SNP rs581553 (c.-106A > G) located in the promoter of POLQ is associated to HBC and bilateral breast cancer.
this SNP is not associated with sporadic breast cancer, but it is associated with HBC, particularly when bilateral breast cancer is considered.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the c.-1060A/G polymorphism of POLQ gene is a potential biomarker for HBOC syndrome.
the c.-1060A/G polymorphism in the POLQ gene is a potential genetic biomarker for HBC, particularly for patients with bilateral breast tumors and HBOC syndrome.
POLQ polymorphisms may contribute to the genetic background of HBC and SBC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
this SNP can be used as a population-based biomarker to identify women at risk for HBC.
the c.-1060A > G polymorphism in POLQ may be used as a new biomarker to identify HBOC patients.
POLQ is a new potential biomarker for hereditary breast cancer and that the rs581553 SNP may be useful in the genetic counseling of patients with HBOC syndrome.
